title: WHEN WE MAKE VOWS TO GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked the Israelites and captured some of them. Then Israel made this vow to the LORD: "If you will deliver these people into our hands, we will totally destroy their cities." - Num 21:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Israel had barely started moving again when trouble arrived. A Canaanite king attacked and even took some of them captive. It was a painful setback, and it would have been easy for the people to panic or grumble as they had done so often before. But this time something is different. Instead of complaining, they turn to the Lord and make a vow.

Notice the honesty of their prayer. They do not pretend to be strong. They simply ask God to deliver the enemy into their hands. There is a quiet maturity here, a growing habit of looking upward before looking around.

A vow is a serious promise made to God, and Scripture treats it with weight. We should be careful never to make promises to God carelessly, thinking we can bargain our way out of a hard moment. Yet there is something beautiful about a people learning, slowly, to bring their fears to the Lord instead of carrying them alone.

When life ambushes you, where do you turn first? The same God who heard Israel in the wilderness invites us to bring every fear to Him through Christ, who has already won the greater battle on our behalf (Heb 4:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is your first instinct when trouble strikes unexpectedly?
2. Are there promises you have made to God that you have forgotten?
3. How can you make turning to God your first response rather than your last?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when life ambushes me, teach me to turn to You first. Help me to bring my fears honestly to You, trusting the victory Jesus has already won. Amen.
